profile.intro: Full-stack dev from Taiwan. Front to back, I build stuff that actually fixes real problems. Walk into the four camps to see what I’ve built.

items.title: Sompisi Transport
items.summary: Travellers couldn’t find or trust this family driving biz online. Now they can — and book it on WhatsApp in a few taps.

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.text: A family-run private driving service in Eswatini. Travellers couldn’t find it online, couldn’t tell if they could trust it, and needed the owner’s number just to book.

chapters.title: What I built
chapters.text: A mobile-first site that names the real owner and driver, lays out the services, and turns the booking form into a pre-filled WhatsApp message to the owner.

chapters.title: Key decision
chapters.text: WhatsApp is the whole back end — no server, no database, $0 to run, and nothing new for the owner to learn. Built as a fully static Nuxt 3 site.

items.sourceNote: Live and working, not promoted yet — so no usage data so far.

items.title: TripTally
items.summary: Splitting trip costs across currencies? Handled — daily budgets, live rates, works offline.

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.text: Splitting travel costs across currencies always ends in a messy group chat and a spreadsheet nobody updates. Most expense apps want an account, a connection and too many taps.

chapters.title: What I built
chapters.text: Tap +, type the amount, one tap for category, one for payment method, date defaults to today — an expense in under 10 seconds. Daily budgets, a spending chart, Chinese / English.

chapters.title: Key decision
chapters.text: The exchange rate is locked in when you log an expense, so old entries never change. Offline, it uses the last known rate and still saves. Data stays in the browser — no sign-up, $0 to run.

items.title: AI-assisted returns for Costco Taiwan
items.summary: Messy return emails → clean cases for staff. Stress-tested on Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT.
items.alt: Redesigned return flow with the AI steps highlighted in red

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.text: Online return requests often arrive incomplete, and staff check each one against six-plus exception rules spread across different policy pages.

chapters.title: What I built
chapters.text: An LLM flow that turns a customer email into a structured case, flags what’s missing and which rules may apply, and drafts the reply — staff keep the final call.

chapters.title: Testing
chapters.text: Ran Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT through the flow against an 11-point checklist to see where each one breaks.

items.sourceNote: Graduate course project, team of four.
